I can see the key change. Before the RIGHT action:
- id=20: color=w, pixels=4, bbox=(38,20)-(39,22) - a 2x2 white block
- id=23: color=g, pixels=1, bbox=(39,22)-(39,22) - a gray pixel to the right
After the RIGHT action:
- id=22: color=w, pixels=4, bbox=(38,23)-(39,25) - the 2x2 white block moved right by 1
- id=24: color=w, pixels=4, bbox=(38,26)-(39,28) - a NEW 2x2 white block appeared
So the RIGHT action caused the small white blocks to the right of the player to extend/move rightward. The player itself didn't move.
This is interesting - it seems like the player is controlling some kind of "beam" or "path" that extends to the right. The small w/g blocks form a horizontal strip.
Let me look at the pattern more carefully. The horizontal strip to the right of the player consists of alternating w (white/light gray) 2x2 blocks and g (gray) single pixels.
Before: w block at (38,17)-(39,19), g at (38,20), w block at (38,20)-(39,22), g at (39,22)
After: w block at (38,17)-(39,19), g at (38,20), w block at (38,20)-(39,22), g at (38,23), w block at (38,23)-(39,25), g at (38,26), w block at (38,26)-(39,28)
So each RIGHT action extends the path by adding another segment (g pixel + w block).
The game area seems to be the dark gray box. The colored blocks (R, b, N) are on the right side. The palette at the bottom shows the order: pink, red, green, blue.
I think the goal might be to extend the path to reach the colored blocks and interact with them in the correct order.
Let me continue exploring by pressing RIGHT more to see what happens when the path reaches the colored blocks.
